newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG STRONG IN BOTH DOWNHILL TRAININGS.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG STRONG IN BOTH DOWNHILL TRAININGS.

text.p: Overall World Cup leader Pernilla Wiberg of Sweden underlined her top form, overcame difficult conditions, and set the pace in downhill training runs on Thursday.
Wiberg clocked the fastest (1:45.85) and second fastest (1:44.06) times in two practice runs for the downhills in Bad Kleinkirchheim on Friday and Saturday.
Friday's race is the replacement for a downhill in Crans Montana which was postponed in December. The Austrian resort will also host a super-G on the same course on Sunday.
Wiberg said conditions on the 3,010 metres long Strohsack course, with a vertical drop of 765 metres, were not ideal and that the piste surface was incredibly bumpy.
"Conditions here remind me of conditions in Crans Montana. But this is the replacement race for Crans, so what else can we expect," said Wiberg, a triple world and twice Olympic champion.
Organisers were forced to postpone a downhill training on Wednesday after warm temperatures had softened the piste and the slope had to be mended with a chemical that hardens snow.
Wiberg's toughest rival in the battle for the overalls, Katja Seizinger of Germany, completed the runs in 20th and 16th places.
"I am not worried about these results. I have been on the circuit for so long, I don't become insecure because of poor training results," said the 1994 Olympic downhill champion.
The second training had to be interrupted for approximately 20 minutes when Tanja Schneider lost control in the upper part and fell. But the Austrian walked away uninjured.
Russia's Varvara Zelenskaya was second quickest in the first practice run (1:46.03) and was trailed by Austria's Michaela Dorfmeister (1:46.10).
Switzerland's Heidi Zurbriggen posted the best second training run time (1:44.06), ahead of Wiberg and Zelenskaya (1:44.63).
